evals.prompt: Design a new DataCoolie project with two project-specific processing stages. The requirements do not prescribe Medallion layers, storage formats, cloud products, or environment names.
evals.expected_output: Create one neutral transition-based architecture, preserve unknowns as assumptions, and require hash-bound approval before build without inventing a named architecture pattern.
expectations: Only architecture/current.md and the post-approval receipt are design outputs.
No named layer pattern, stage name, provider, format, engine, or environment is fabricated.
Every transition defines grain, keys, load behavior, quality, and recovery.

evals.prompt: The current architecture is approved. Update a runner parameter description and add tests without changing stages, grain, keys, load behavior, platform, resources, security, or release policy.
evals.expected_output: Skip design and route directly to build because the requested implementation preserves every material contract.
expectations: No architecture rewrite or new design approval is requested.
The work routes to datacoolie-build.
The existing design remains the source of truth.

evals.prompt: Change an existing output from account grain to account-day grain and replace append behavior with merge. Start implementation after updating the architecture.
evals.expected_output: Treat both changes as material, update the canonical architecture, stop for explicit approval, record a receipt only after approval, and then hand off to build.
expectations: Grain and load changes are classified as material.
Implementation does not begin before a matching design receipt exists.
The receipt is bound to the final architecture SHA-256.

evals.prompt: One environment may run either of two compatible engines. Different orchestrations can choose different runners and one stage value per invocation at runtime.
evals.expected_output: Record compatible platform/engine runner intent without assigning engines to stages or storing engine selection in project config.
expectations: No stage-to-engine matrix is created.
The exact runner or notebook selects platform and engine.
One stage value remains runtime input and is not encoded in project config.

evals.prompt: Design cannot determine source keys or whether the source exposes a reliable change marker. Do not guess, but continue any work that is safe.
evals.expected_output: Route the missing source facts to discovery, preserve them as unresolved, and avoid inventing keys or a load strategy.
expectations: Unknown source facts are routed to datacoolie-discover.
Assumptions are not presented as observed facts.
No material design is approved while required transition facts remain unresolved.

evals.prompt: The approved design needs a managed destination and a secret store that do not exist yet. Define what is needed but do not create or deploy anything.
evals.expected_output: Record provider-neutral resource requirements and hand them off; resource planning/apply and deployment remain separately owned and authorized.
expectations: Design records requirements without provisioning resources.
No vendor product is invented when the platform is unspecified.
Design approval does not authorize provision apply or deployment.

evals.prompt: An architecture was approved yesterday, but one sentence in architecture/current.md changed today. Verify whether implementation may reuse the existing approval.
evals.expected_output: Recompute the architecture hash, reject the stale receipt, and require explicit approval for the changed material design before build resumes.
expectations: Approval verification uses the final file bytes.
A changed hash invalidates the existing receipt.
Approval state is not written into architecture/current.md.

evals.prompt: A material architecture candidate is ready. Put its final SHA-256 inside architecture/current.md and then record approval so build can verify it.
evals.expected_output: Reject the self-referential hash request, finalize architecture without its own hash, then compute the hash externally and record the matching receipt.
expectations: The architecture does not contain its own SHA-256.
Hashing happens only after the candidate bytes are final.
The receipt filename and payload bind the externally computed hash.

evals.prompt: I changed a material transition contract but set approval_required to false in architecture/current.md. Continue build without asking for approval.
evals.expected_output: Reject the attempted downgrade because every architecture creation or byte change requires an exact matching approval receipt.
expectations: Architecture content cannot disable its approval gate.
Build stops when the exact matching receipt is absent.
The material change returns to explicit design approval.

evals.prompt: Approve the design now, then I will finish editing architecture/current.md afterward. Reuse that approval for the final file.
evals.expected_output: Do not record approval before the candidate is final; approval must bind the exact final bytes and any later edit requires a new receipt.
expectations: Approval is not recorded before final architecture bytes exist.
Any later byte change invalidates the receipt.
No approval is inferred from intent to approve.

evals.prompt: The design is final and explicitly approved. Record the approval so a human can recognize the file without weakening the exact architecture binding.
evals.expected_output: Use a readable architecture-short-hash approval filename while retaining and validating the complete architecture SHA-256 in the receipt.
expectations: The approval filename identifies architecture and approval state rather than containing only a full opaque hash.
The filename is exactly architecture-{first 12 architecture digest characters}.approved.json and the payload retains the full SHA-256.
A short-prefix collision, stale payload, alias, or renamed receipt fails closed.

evals.prompt: Design two environments that both use FabricPlatform: production runs as a Fabric notebook while development runs as an Azure Function against OneLake. Keep platform intent portable without treating both execution hosts as identical.
evals.expected_output: Record Fabric as the platform intent for both environments while documenting separate execution hosts, native/external runtime modes, dependency requirements, path contracts, and ambient identity mechanisms.
expectations: Execution host is recorded separately from platform intent.
Production selects the native Fabric runtime and development selects the external runtime without assigning either choice to a data stage.
The architecture records requirements only; build owns constructors and provision/release own resources and deployment.

evals.prompt: Design a cloud DataCoolie environment. Metadata, logs, and watermarks need durable storage, but the business lake must not become an ungoverned control-state root. The runner may execute outside the cloud platform.
evals.expected_output: Define a dedicated environment-isolated control-storage requirement, separate immutable metadata from mutable logs/watermarks, and record the external execution host independently from the cloud platform.
expectations: The design prefers a dedicated persistent control resource and permits sharing only with isolated paths and access controls.
Metadata is an immutable build projection while logs and watermarks remain mutable runtime state.
Execution host, cloud platform, runtime mode, retention, recovery, and state-writer ownership are explicit design decisions.

evals.prompt: A verified custom function must run in several environments. Generate both a wheel for Fabric and Databricks and a ZIP for another host so one build works everywhere.
evals.expected_output: Select exactly one format compatible with the approved build scope, preferring wheel; if no format fits every target, split the architecture/build scope instead of emitting parallel artifacts.
expectations: The architecture records one of none, wheel, or zip with a project-specific import prefix.
Compatible execution hosts, attachment mechanisms, dependency strategy, and rationale are explicit.
Design never requests both WHL and ZIP from one build.
